## Overview

This notebook starts applying the cell-cell communication analysis established in `06`-`08` (LIANA+, significant ligand-receptor pairs per `spatial_pair`) to the STARmap PLUS single-cell-resolution dataset built in `09` (hippocampus only, control mice, 8 vs 13 months).

For now this is deliberately just the first check, not an analysis yet: `06`/`07`/`08` all work from the union of ligand/receptor genes across every significant LR pair in `significant_lr_pairs.csv` -- the "57 significant genes" referenced throughout those notebooks. STARmap PLUS is a targeted panel (~2,766 genes plus a 64-gene validation panel), not whole-transcriptome, so there's no guarantee it actually contains every one of those genes. Checking that directly, before building any LR-scoring logic on top of it, is the point of this file -- same "diagnose first" approach as `09`.

```{r setup}
#| label: setup
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(Seurat)

out_dir  <- "starmap_plus_processed"  # same out_dir 09 saves into
hpc_path <- file.path(out_dir, "starmap_plus_control_seurat_hippocampus.rds")
```

## Load the 57-gene significant LR set (from 06/07/08)

Same construction as `08`'s `rebuild-lr-genes-long` chunk: split each significant pair's `ligand_complex`/`receptor_complex` on `"_"` (multi-subunit complexes), then take the union across every `spatial_pair`.

```{r load-lr-genes}
#| label: load-lr-genes

split_complex <- function(x) strsplit(x, "_")

sig_pairs <- read.csv("significant_lr_pairs.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
  distinct(spatial_pair, ligand_complex, receptor_complex)

lr_gene_sets <- purrr::pmap(sig_pairs, function(spatial_pair, ligand_complex, receptor_complex) {
  ligands   <- unlist(split_complex(ligand_complex))
  receptors <- unlist(split_complex(receptor_complex))
  unique(c(ligands, receptors))
})

significant_genes <- sort(unique(unlist(lr_gene_sets)))

cat("Significant LR gene set size:", length(significant_genes), "\n")
print(significant_genes)
```

## Load the STARmap PLUS hippocampus object (from 09)

```{r load-hippocampus}
#| label: load-hippocampus

starmap_hpc <- readRDS(hpc_path)
cat("starmap_hpc:", nrow(starmap_hpc), "genes x", ncol(starmap_hpc), "cells\n")
```

## Merge SMC + Endo into "Vascular" (matching the 06-08 reference taxonomy)

`06`-`08`'s cell-type vocabulary merged `SMC`/`Pericyte`/`Endothelial` into one `Vascular` label (see `03`'s `Celltype_updated`). STARmap PLUS's `top_level_cell_type` keeps `SMC` and `Endo` as separate categories (no `Pericyte` label in this panel's annotation), so the same merge is applied here -- `celltype_merged` is a new column, `top_level_cell_type` itself is left untouched.

```{r merge-vascular}
#| label: merge-vascular

starmap_hpc$celltype_merged <- starmap_hpc$top_level_cell_type
starmap_hpc$celltype_merged[starmap_hpc$celltype_merged %in% c("SMC", "Endo")] <- "Vascular"

cat("top_level_cell_type counts (before merge):\n")
print(table(starmap_hpc$top_level_cell_type))
cat("\ncelltype_merged counts (SMC + Endo -> Vascular):\n")
print(table(starmap_hpc$celltype_merged))

saveRDS(starmap_hpc, file.path(out_dir, "starmap_plus_control_seurat_hippocampus_merged.rds"))
```

## Gene panel overlap

```{r gene-overlap}
#| label: gene-overlap

panel_genes <- rownames(starmap_hpc)

present_genes <- intersect(significant_genes, panel_genes)
missing_genes <- setdiff(significant_genes, panel_genes)

cat("Of the", length(significant_genes), "significant LR genes:\n")
cat(" - present in the STARmap PLUS panel:", length(present_genes), "\n")
cat(" - missing from the panel:", length(missing_genes), "\n\n")

# Case-insensitive check as a sanity guard: if this count is a lot higher than the
# exact-match count above, the gap is a capitalization mismatch between gene symbol
# conventions (e.g. "Gfap" vs "GFAP"), not genes that are genuinely absent.
present_ci <- intersect(toupper(significant_genes), toupper(panel_genes))
cat("(Case-insensitive match count for comparison:", length(present_ci),
    "-- a gap between this and the exact-match count above points at a capitalization",
    "mismatch, not real absence.)\n\n")

if (length(present_genes) > 0) {
  cat("Present:\n")
  print(present_genes)
}
if (length(missing_genes) > 0) {
  cat("\nMissing:\n")
  print(missing_genes)
}
```

## Keep only LR pairs where both sides are fully present

A pair only survives if *every* gene on both sides is in the panel -- for a multi-subunit complex (e.g. a ligand made of two genes joined by `"_"`), that means all of its subunits, not just one, since a partial complex can't actually be scored.

```{r filter-sig-pairs}
#| label: filter-sig-pairs

gene_all_present <- function(complex_str) {
  genes <- unlist(split_complex(complex_str))
  all(genes %in% panel_genes)
}

ligand_ok   <- vapply(sig_pairs$ligand_complex, gene_all_present, logical(1))
receptor_ok <- vapply(sig_pairs$receptor_complex, gene_all_present, logical(1))

sig_pairs_present <- sig_pairs[ligand_ok & receptor_ok, ]

cat("LR pairs kept (both ligand and receptor fully present in the panel):",
    nrow(sig_pairs_present), "/", nrow(sig_pairs), "\n\n")
cat("Kept, by spatial_pair:\n")
print(table(sig_pairs_present$spatial_pair))
cat("\nOriginal, by spatial_pair (for comparison):\n")
print(table(sig_pairs$spatial_pair))

sig_pairs_present
```

## Looking for candidate signaling-relay chains

The goal here is a *directional* relay -- cell type A signals to B, and B (not just "B in the neighborhood") itself relays a signal on to C -- which `06`-`08`'s LR pairs can only suggest a starting point for, not confirm outright: those pairs come from a different cell-type vocabulary than STARmap PLUS uses.

```{r celltype-vocab-check}
#| label: celltype-vocab-check

original_pairs <- unique(sig_pairs_present$spatial_pair)
cat("spatial_pair values in sig_pairs_present:\n")
print(original_pairs)

pair_celltypes <- strsplit(original_pairs, "-")
names(pair_celltypes) <- original_pairs

bad_splits <- pair_celltypes[lengths(pair_celltypes) != 2]
if (length(bad_splits) > 0) {
  cat("\nspatial_pair values that didn't split into exactly 2 tokens on '-' (check by eye):\n")
  print(bad_splits)
}

original_celltypes <- sort(unique(unlist(pair_celltypes)))
cat("\nCell-type vocabulary used in spatial_pair (the ORIGINAL Visium/RCTD/Jessberger-reference analysis, from 06-08):\n")
print(original_celltypes)

cat("\nCell-type vocabulary in starmap_hpc$top_level_cell_type (STARmap PLUS, raw):\n")
print(sort(unique(starmap_hpc$top_level_cell_type)))

cat("\nCell-type vocabulary in starmap_hpc$celltype_merged (STARmap PLUS, SMC+Endo merged to Vascular):\n")
print(sort(unique(starmap_hpc$celltype_merged)))

cat("\nCell-type vocabulary in starmap_hpc$sub_level_cell_type (STARmap PLUS, finer-grained):\n")
print(sort(unique(starmap_hpc$sub_level_cell_type)))
```

`celltype_merged` now shares the `Vascular` label with `06`-`08`'s vocabulary directly, closing part of the gap -- but the rest still needs an explicit mapping: `06`-`08`'s `GC`, `Neurogenic_lineage`, `Cajal-Retzius`, etc. don't have obvious 1:1 matches in STARmap's `top_level_cell_type` (`DG` is the closest to `GC`, but that's an assumption to confirm, not a given), so each cell type named in a candidate `spatial_pair` still needs to be checked against STARmap's labels above (and `sub_level_cell_type`, which may resolve some of these better than the top-level categories do) before trusting any chain match.

```{r print-sig-pairs-detail}
#| label: print-sig-pairs-detail

sig_pairs_present |>
  arrange(spatial_pair) |>
  select(spatial_pair, ligand_complex, receptor_complex)
```

## Export for downstream use

```{r export-sig-pairs}
#| label: export-sig-pairs

write.csv(sig_pairs_present, file.path(out_dir, "sig_pairs_present_starmap.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Notes on interpretation

`present_genes` is the ceiling on what any STARmap PLUS-based LR reanalysis can actually test with the same significant-pair gene set `06`-`08` used -- any `spatial_pair`/function whose contributing genes fall entirely in `missing_genes` simply can't be evaluated on this panel and would need to be dropped or substituted before going further. If the case-insensitive count in `gene-overlap` comes out noticeably higher than the exact-match count, that's worth fixing first (e.g. `toupper()`/`tools::toTitleCase()` normalization on one side) rather than treating those genes as absent.

`sig_pairs_present` is the actual usable subset -- the LR pairs whose full gene requirement (both sides, every subunit of a multi-gene complex) is met by this panel. That's what any next step (scoring these pairs' spatial expression/co-localization in `starmap_hpc`) should build from, not the original unfiltered `sig_pairs`.
